summary: Heaven & Ale has you moving a shared rondel-like track to gather ingredients and monks while carefully layering colored barrel tiles to maximize scoring runs. It's a tight, efficient engine game where spatial puzzle-solving on your barrel board matters as much as resource collection.
praised: elegant tension between garden expansion and harvesting
criticised: rondel/turn-order mechanism can feel fiddly at first
barrel scoring math takes a game or two to click
limited direct player interaction beyond spot competition

interaction.kind: shared action selection, private tableau building
interaction.detail: Players pick from a shared row of action/resource spaces that becomes temporarily unavailable once taken, so timing and blocking of these common spots is the main way opponents affect each other. The actual construction — garden tiles and barrel filling — happens entirely on each player's own separate board, with no attacks or negotiation.

scoring.how_you_win: You brew barrels whose value is capped by the weakest resource underneath them, so you win by keeping your garden's resource tracks evenly developed rather than maxed in one; add monastery tile bonuses at the end for the highest total.
